skill.name: openserv-multi-agent-workflows
skill.description: Build and document OpenServ workflows that coordinate multiple agents through triggers, tasks, dependencies, edges, payments, and platform APIs.
skill.summary: Practical OpenServ patterns for designing, provisioning, and operating multi-agent workflows.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The 400 static matches are predominantly documentation noise for template literals, diagrams, documented endpoints, and conventional environment-variable configuration. Two direct wallet-private-key references are confirmed security-sensitive, and the workflow examples also lack verification before assigning work to marketplace agents. Static review was capped at 400/444 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 44 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Wallet private keys are used for client authentication and on-chain registration.
remediation.suggestion: Use a secret manager, keep keys out of repositories and logs, fund a dedicated least-privilege wallet, and document key rotation and compromise response.

remediation.issue: Marketplace search results are accepted by position without trust validation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin agent identifiers and versions where possible, verify publisher identity and capabilities, review permissions and data handling, and test agents with non-sensitive inputs.

remediation.issue: Webhook and paid-trigger examples can expose workflow invocation and incur costs.
remediation.suggestion: Protect trigger tokens, require authentication and rate limits, set spending caps, and monitor repeated or unexpected invocations.

remediation.issue: The documentation recommends update and install commands that can change local skill content.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package and repository revisions, review changes before installation, and run updates in an isolated environment.

content.value_statement: Complex agent projects need clear data flow, dependencies, and reliable triggers. This skill provides practical OpenServ patterns for building and operating coordinated workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explain OpenServ workflow containers, tasks, triggers, dependencies, and graph edges.
Provide TypeScript examples using Platform Client methods and workflow synchronization.
Show marketplace agent discovery and task assignment patterns.
Demonstrate webhook and x402 trigger setup, activation, and invocation.
Cover workflow monitoring, updates, provisioning, and common troubleshooting steps.
limitations: It provides examples and guidance, but it does not execute workflows or call OpenServ APIs.
API behavior, SDK names, and platform features may change after the examples were written.
Users must supply valid OpenServ credentials, agent identifiers, and platform access.
Examples do not verify marketplace agent trust, output quality, pricing, or data handling.

use_cases.title: Plan a Content Pipeline
use_cases.description: Design a sequential workflow that researches a topic, writes content, and sends results through explicit task edges.

use_cases.title: Launch a Paid Agent Service
use_cases.description: Adapt provisioning and x402 examples to expose a paid workflow with wallet configuration and clear task sequencing.

use_cases.title: Debug Workflow Execution
use_cases.description: Use the reference and troubleshooting guidance to inspect triggers, dependencies, workspace agents, and synchronization behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how OpenServ workflows, agents, tasks, triggers, dependencies, and edges fit together for a beginner.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Sequential Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an OpenServ workflow for [goal]. Define the agents, task order, inputs, outputs, trigger, and edges.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an Example
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the most relevant example for [use case]. Preserve explicit data flow, validate required agents, and list configuration changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turning documentation into a project plan

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this OpenServ workflow design for security, reliability, cost control, agent trust, webhook exposure, and failure handling. Return prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a two-agent workflow that researches a topic and drafts a blog post.
output_examples.output: A sequential design with a webhook trigger, research task, writing task, explicit trigger-to-research and research-to-writing edges, and required inputs.

output_examples.input: Why does a task not start after its dependency completes?
output: Confirm that the dependency status is done.
Check that the workflow graph contains an edge from the prior task to the waiting task.
Verify that both tasks reference agents present in the workspace.

output_examples.input: How should I expose a paid OpenServ workflow?
output_examples.output: Use an x402 trigger, configure a payout wallet, authenticate the client securely, activate the trigger, and test payment and task execution separately.

best_practices: Use explicit edges to express intentional data flow between triggers and tasks.
Keep tasks focused and validate marketplace agents before assigning them work or sensitive inputs.
Protect wallet credentials, test paid triggers with limits, and monitor workflow state after synchronization.
anti_patterns: Connecting every task to every other task without a clear data dependency.
Selecting the first marketplace search result without checking identity, capability, trust, or cost.
Committing wallet keys to a repository or exposing webhook tokens without access controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design OpenServ workflows where agents execute coordinated tasks through triggers, dependencies, and graph edges.

faq.question: Does it execute the examples for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and TypeScript examples. You must install dependencies, configure credentials, and run the client.

faq.question: Why are workflow edges important?
faq.answer: Edges connect triggers and tasks in the execution graph. Task dependencies alone may not create the required data flow.

faq.question: Can I use paid x402 triggers?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples explain x402 trigger setup, payout wallet resolution, payment calls, and paywall URLs.

faq.question: How should I protect wallet credentials?
faq.answer: Keep private keys outside source control, use a secret manager, limit wallet funds, and avoid sending keys to agents or webhooks.

faq.question: Is every marketplace agent safe to use?
faq.answer: No. Review agent identity, permissions, inputs, outputs, pricing, and data handling before connecting an external agent.
